§0.3 states the goal and nine tasks.

findings.detail: The document states the project's own contribution explicitly: the layer above the model (orchestration, validation, access control, plan lifecycle).

evidence.text: Приносът на разработката е в слоя над модела – оркестрацията на агентите, проверката на изхода, контрола на достъпа и жизнения цикъл на действията.

findings.detail: §0.2 problem, §0.3 goal, §0.7 expected results.

Own logic is described in depth: context packets (§2.8.8), Zod schema validation and JSON repair (§2.8.7), tool loop with per-call authorisation (§2.8.3), draft-confirm-apply with plan hash (§2.8.5). Verified in src/server/llm.
Data origin is described: workspace data from the database, user-uploaded PDF/text documents, and a hand-written 55-case set for evaluation.
Preparation is described: PDF text extraction, overlapping chunking with page numbers, embeddings, context packets and rolling summaries.
Use of data is described: retrieval (hybrid search) with citations, domain-limited context per agent.
55 test cases with two metrics and a confusion matrix are presented (§2.14).

The conclusions drawn from the evaluation are only that the offline run passes 55/55 and that its scope is limited. No weakness of the solution's real behaviour is identified, although the repo holds live results that show them (routing 72.7%, tool-argument validity 70.6%; persona run: replies in the wrong language to Latin-script Bulgarian, invented entities, event times saved in UTC).

evidence.text: Всичките 55 случая преминават и двете проверки…

crosscheck.claim: Only offline results; no weaknesses identified
crosscheck.contradiction: Weaknesses were measured but are not reported.

findings.detail: Chapter 1 explains the concepts in the author's own words.
§0.5 and §2.14.1 explain the limits: non-determinism, no own training, embeddings dependency.
§1.5 (hallucinations) and §1.2 (non-determinism) explain wrong answers and mitigation.
§2.16 discusses bias in language models.
§1.5, §2.11.3 and §2.16 discuss confidentiality, locked notes excluded from context and GDPR.
§2.17 gives the public URL, the GitHub repository and test accounts.

Nothing in the document allows reproduction: no system requirements (Node 22, pnpm 10, PostgreSQL with pgvector), no install steps, no list of required environment variables (LLM_PROVIDER and the provider key, database URL, auth secrets, optional Redis/Stripe/Resend/UploadThing/VAPID), no migration or start commands. The URL and repo link let someone use or download the project but not run it.

crosscheck.contradiction: The repo has everything needed for a setup section, but the document does not include one.

findings.detail: The LLM is presented explicitly as one interchangeable component behind an OpenAI-compatible client (§1.2, §2.8, §2.8.11).
Input processing (context packets, page context, summarisation) and output processing (Zod validation, repair, authorisation, plan hashing) are described.

The reported evaluation measures only the code around the model: the offline run feeds hand-written answers instead of the model, and the document states that the live mode was not measured. That is the 'липса на … анализ на резултатите' case in т. 2.3. The repo already has the missing measurement: live routing eval on 2026-09-25 (gpt-oss-20b) with 72.7% routing accuracy, 96.4%/98.2% schema validity before/after repair, 76.5% tool selection, p50 10.3 s; and a persona evaluation on 2026-10-17 (44 turns, 2 of 9 criteria fully met).

evidence.text: Той не измерва дали моделът произвежда такъв отговор; това е предмет на живия режим, който … не е включен в настоящите резултати.

crosscheck.contradiction: Live results exist in the repo and are omitted.

findings.detail: The choice of a pretrained API model, the OpenAI-compatible format and the provider abstraction are justified (§1.2, §2.8.11, §1.8). Weak spot: no reason is given for DeepSeek V4 Flash specifically, and the evaluations in the repo used gpt-oss-20b.
